the interaction of two common detergents, polysorbate 80 and polysorbate 60 with different proteins.
the interaction of the detergent polysorbate 80 with different model proteins and the effect on protein stability.
the interaction of polysorbitan detergents with different proteins and the effect of the detergente–protein interaction on the thermal stability of the protein.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the stabilisation of proteins by detergents can be attributed to the stabilisation of the protein surface and the hydrophobic interactions of the protein with the hydrophobic part of the detergent.
the detergents are able to bind to BSA, but the binding is not sufficient to stabilise the proteins from aggregation.
the stabilising effects of polysorbate are protein specific and depend on the binding constant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the detergents bind with a low affinity to proteins with a low binding enthalpy and a small change in entropy upon binding.
the binding of the detergens to BSA has an impact on the stability, whereas the interaction of the detergants to lysozyme or the immunoglobulin does not.
the detergents bind with low affinity and low specificity to BSA and that they induce a weak thermal stabilisation.

the stabilising effect of the detergent is not only due to the interaction between the protein and the detergent but rather the interaction with the solvent.
